newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends $13.75 lower, crack sheds $1.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends $13.75 lower, crack sheds $1.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed dramatically lower on Thursday, pulling crude down in its wake, in a correction to the scorching gains of the last two weeks, brokers said.
Nov gas oil, the new front month, closed down $13.75 a tonne at $224.50.
"We were overdone on the upside...we were just waiting for the downside to come," said one IPE floor broker.
Nov Brent had shed 65 cents by 1648 GMT to trade at $23.62 a barrel, four cents above the day's low.
Despite losses, Brent still outperformed gas oil, narrowing the Nov crack spread by $1 to $6.50 a barrel.
Some traders said that reports that tertiary stocks of heating oil in the key German market stood at 65 percent of capacity were bullish.
Although this was six percent lower than a historical average, traders said the market was expecting a lower number.
Big losses on NYMEX heating oil also encouraged the downward correction, but some brokers said that gas oil was the market leader.
"We weren't playing copy cat, European products took the lead on the upside, so this is what you'd expect," a broker said.
Frenetic profit-taking on Oct gas oil ahead of its expiry this morning played an important part in triggering the move, brokers said.
